items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The patch is the same as the reference: a short conditional with a clear comment explaining why the auth is added back ('parse_url doesn't provide the netloc with auth'). It follows the existing style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Small 4-line change inside the existing function. It reuses the `auth` value that parse_url already returns. No new helpers, no dead code, no debug leftovers.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The `if auth:` guard means URLs without credentials behave as before. Nothing new can raise, there are no magic constants and no hardcoded credentials. Hidden tests pass (F2P 2/2, P2P 185/185).

items.name: prepend_scheme_if_needed public behaviour unchanged otherwise
items.name_zh: prepend_scheme_if_needed 其他公开行为不变
items.evidence: Signature unchanged. Only adds `netloc = '@'.join([auth, netloc])` using parse_url's own auth field, so credentials keep their original encoding. No urllib3 pinning or Python-version check. The agent checked that the existing scheme-less and host:port cases still pass.
